clue.text: Old timer's incentive?

definitions.meaning: belonging to an old clock or watch, whose coiled driving spring keeps it going
the chief motive or driving force behind an action

explanation.definitionFit: The coiled spring powering a clockwork mechanism, and figuratively the principal driving motive behind anything.

clue.text: Bill left to settle

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill to be paid
quit means left, departed

explanation.surface: Someone owes money and walks out rather than pay what is due.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settle' here is the old sense of discharging a debt, as in acquitting oneself of an obligation.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquit a debt is an archaic way of saying to pay it off or discharge it.

clue.text: One's having to take an external degree — what a bother!

indicators.note: the degree word takes the other piece inside it, wrapping it like an outer layer

parts.note: a nuance is a slight degree of difference
one is I, and the 's adds S, giving IS

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about having to study for a distance-learning qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'External degree' reads as a distance-learning qualification; here 'degree' means a subtle shade of difference, and 'external' is the wrapping signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation at some annoyance: a pest or irritant is exactly that kind of trouble.

clue.text: Way of following Times pieces across the country

definitions.text: Way of following Times pieces across the country

parts.words: Way of following Times pieces across the country
parts.note: a cross-country game in which runners track a trail of torn newspaper scraps, the Times standing for any newspaper

explanation.definitionFit: A hare-and-hounds race where pursuers follow a trail of scattered scraps over open land.

clue.text: State of Cochise, for example, Apache leader

parts.note: Cochise was a chief of the Apache, a Native American, here an Indian in old usage

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Cochise is described as the chief of the Apache people.
explanation.walkthrough: Cochise was a 19th-century Apache chief; 'leader' takes only the first letter of Apache.
explanation.definitionFit: A Midwestern US state, one of the fifty.

clue.text: Cheek sore?

definitions.meaning: a painful swelling or chafed patch on the skin, especially of a horse

explanation.definitionFit: Both impudent nerve and a skin abrasion caused by rubbing share this short word.

clue.text: Semi-nude costume ball?

indicators.note: semi- means half, so take the second half of the word nude

parts.note: livery is a distinctive uniform or costume worn by servants

explanation.surface: Someone attends a fancy-dress dance in a half-naked outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ball' looks like a dance to go with costume and nude, but it is a bowled ball in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket each bowled ball is called a delivery.

clue.text: Divine robin heard in ministry

annotationWithheld.why: Divine robin heard in ministry (10): PRIEST (Divine) + HOOD, but no honest parse makes 'robin heard' give HOOD by sound, so a word seems to be doing two jobs or the clue is misprinted

clue.text: Attend a quiet conference, for example

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
Conference is a well-known variety of pear

explanation.surface: Someone is told to show up at a low-key meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conference' looks like a meeting; it is the Conference pear, a common British variety.
explanation.definitionFit: To be present, as when one turns up in court or at an event.

clue.text: Suitably kitted out England's opener made a reply

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, like an opening batsman

parts.note: quipped means made a witty reply

explanation.surface: England's opening batsman, properly padded up, gives a smart answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the necessary gear or kit fitted out for a task.

clue.text: Throw light on one row about a chimney

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: about means going round, so the row word surrounds the chimney word

parts.note: a line is a row
lum is a Scots word for a chimney

explanation.surface: Someone shines a light on a line of rooftops round a chimney stack.
explanation.walkthrough: LUM is a Scottish chimney, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: To light up or illuminate, literally or by explaining.

clue.text: Bananas going the wrong way take one's breath away

indicators.note: going the wrong way means reading the word backwards

parts.note: bananas means crazy, nuts

explanation.surface: A display of bananas turned upside down astonishes an onlooker.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish or daze someone so they are left speechless.

clue.text: Cock-eyed bishop in mass trial freed

indicators.note: freed suggests the letters are let loose and rearranged

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop is released after a mass trial and is looking rather askew.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to a squint, the condition in which the eyes do not align.

clue.text: Meeting work-unit in nunnery

indicators.note: in places the work unit inside the nunnery word

parts.note: a convent is a nunnery
the erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: A work team assembles inside a convent.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming together at a point, as lines that converge do.

clue.text: Mark is one leaving set to be repaired

indicators.note: something to be repaired is put back together differently, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A man named Mark is departing, leaving a broken set to be fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark is the author of the second Gospel.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Mark wrote one of the four Gospels, so he is a Gospel writer.

clue.text: Stock procedure, to use channel to mill

parts.note: a race is a stock or breed, a line of descent
a way is a method or procedure

explanation.surface: A method for using a channel to carry water to a mill.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill race, the watercourse that feeds a water wheel.

clue.text: Ground squirrel, playful imp in one piece

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the piece word

parts.note: a chunk is one piece

indicators.note: playful suggests the letters frolic into a new order

explanation.surface: A mischievous imp is part of a ground squirrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground squirrel' is the definition: the North American chipmunk is a burrowing, ground-dwelling member of the squirrel family.
explanation.definitionFit: A small striped North American burrowing rodent of the squirrel family.

clue.text: Call up when getting near to quarry…

definitions.text: Call up when getting near to quarry

parts.words: Call up when getting near to quarry
parts.note: the cry a fox-hunter raises on sighting the fox

explanation.definitionFit: A hunting cry given when the fox is spotted.

clue.text: He may know many words for heather on Scottish island

parts.note: ling is common heather
Uist is an island in the Outer Hebrides

explanation.surface: Someone knows many words for heather on a Hebridean island.
explanation.definitionFit: A person fluent in several languages, with a large vocabulary.

clue.text: Chronicles of girl stars

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
Aries is a constellation of stars

explanation.surface: Accounts of a girl's astrological stars.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal journals record events day by day, much as a chronicle does.

clue.text: … cheerful call, but hopeless!

parts.note: blithe means cheerful
to ring someone is to call them

explanation.surface: A hunter's cry follows on, cheerful but useless.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 17, a hunting call, so 'call' wants to be a shout; it is a phone ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Utterly foolish or useless, as in a blithering idiot.

clue.text: Aromatic oil from northern Ardennes

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: A fragrant oil produced in the northern Ardennes.
explanation.definitionFit: Spikenard, a fragrant ointment from an Indian plant.

clue.text: Antonio's news centre?

parts.note: in The Merchant of Venice, Antonio's merchant circle asks what news there is on the Venetian bridge and exchange

explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's line 'What news on the ...?' refers to the Venetian bridge where merchants traded.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian bridge and business quarter where merchants exchanged news.

clue.text: Term sees development of its American counterpart

indicators.note: a development of letters develops them into a new form, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A school term is seen to evolve into its American equivalent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Term' looks like the definition; it is fodder, and the definition is 'its American counterpart', the US name for a term.
explanation.definitionFit: American colleges divide the academic year into two halves rather than three terms.

clue.text: Exclamation of disapproval when shut out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone tuts in disapproval at being locked out.
explanation.definitionFit: An old interjection expressing impatience or scorn, like pshaw.

clue.text: How writer endorses letters of introduction?

definitions.meaning: a writer may sign a document with just the first letters of the names
the letters that begin, or introduce, each name or word

explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviated signatures formed from the first letters of one's names, which also open each word.

clue.text: Badgers making a sound we can hear

indicators.note: we can hear signals that the words are spoken aloud

parts.note: a sound is a noise

explanation.surface: Badgers making a sound that people nearby can hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badgers' looks like the animals, but it is a verb meaning pesters.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger is to pester or irritate persistently.

clue.text: Indecision apparent in Tahiti's one resort?

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means sort again, rearranging the letters

parts.note: taken as written, including the S

explanation.surface: Being unable to decide on a holiday resort in Tahiti.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday spot, but read as re-sort it rearranges TAHITIS and ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pausing or wavering before acting shows irresolution.
